correctness.rationale: The exact criterion is necessary and sufficient: two pure-token vertices share only mixed-token neighbors, so the selected mixed-token matrix needs at most one empty row and one empty column; a mixed token is adjacent to selected pure tokens exactly when its A endpoint or B endpoint is covered, forcing a complete edge cover on A or on B. The selected parts therefore factor. Two independent inclusion-exclusion formulas give every coefficient. A minimum selected mixed part has \(n-1\) cells, one in every column but one; the function from active columns to rows must use \(m\) or \(m-1\) rows. Minimum pure selection is a minimum edge cover of the smaller part, or either part if their cover sizes tie. For even part size this is a perfect matching, for odd part size one 3-path plus a matching; exact multiplicities yield the stated Stirling-number coefficient. The formulas and edge-cover counts are independently reproduced by a standalone standard-library verifier, including 4,260,928 literally enumerated token-graph vertex subsets. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary 2026 papers prove ordinary closed-neighborhood domination numbers, not the total open-neighborhood polynomial or exact all-size enumeration. The ordinary parameter differs by one in documented exceptional cases and cannot imply the claimed total-domination polynomial. A different historical title or a presently inaccessible source could still contain an equivalent formula; priority is qualified, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The closely related new literature determines ordinary domination on this two-parameter infinite token-graph family; its stricter total-domination polynomial is a natural next invariant and is not reducible to its published scalar minimum. The result enumerates every total-dominating vertex set by size via two independent structural factors, determines the exact minimum and a Stirling-number formula for the number of minimum configurations, and exhibits parameter regimes in which ordinary versus total minima differ. These facts support studying covering redundancy and distributions of feasible token configurations, without requiring a downstream theorem.
